key_insight: A neural-network subgrid model can learn unresolved magnetic-turbulence effects in special relativistic magnetohydrodynamics and reproduce higher-resolution behavior in low-resolution simulations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to accelerate large-eddy simulations of neutron star mergers, accretion disks, and other relativistic plasma flows where direct resolution of small-scale instabilities is too expensive.
method: Train a neural network as a subgrid closure for special relativistic MHD.
Use it in online large-eddy simulations of the 3D Kelvin-Helmholtz instability.
Compare against higher-resolution simulations with both a priori and a posteriori tests.
evidence_signal: In a low-resolution run, the model captured magnetic field amplification comparable to a simulation at 4× higher resolution and achieved a 44× speed-up.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on one instability test, so robustness and generalization to broader relativistic turbulence and full merger simulations still need validation.
paper_title: Subgrid Modelling for Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics with Machine Learning
